# Protocol fixtures

`tools.json`, `state-running.ru.md` and `breakpoints.ru.md` are synthetic, non-sensitive fixtures projected from the official Vanessa Automation tag `1.2.043.45`. They are not live captures. `tools.json` preserves names, property types and required flags for the selected control, client, form, authoring and diagnostic tools, including `load_features` (also checked in the live tools/list capture); descriptions and unrelated tools are omitted.

Sources:
- https://github.com/Pr-Mex/vanessa-automation/blob/1.2.043.45/VanessaAutomation/Forms/MCPVA_Служебный/Ext/Form/Module.bsl
- https://github.com/Pr-Mex/vanessa-automation/blob/1.2.043.45/VanessaAutomation/Forms/MCPVA/Ext/Form/Module.bsl

Unknown/localized output is deliberately reported as unknown until its exact format has been verified. Source fixtures do not certify any installed EPF/devkit version or live execution.

`tools.live.json` and `state-idle.live.ru.md` were captured on 2026-10-17 from the EPF in 1cDrive's `develop` tree (Vanessa UI reports `1.2.043.45`), client_mcp `0.6.6`, WebTransport `0.6.4`, 1C Windows `8.5.1.1522`. MCP handshake reports `rmcp 1.1.0`; tools/list returned 48 tools. The fixture keeps only the selected schemas and omits descriptions/unrelated tools. The idle state had no open feature or test client; its workspace path is replaced with `<WORKSPACE>`. These captures verify connection/capabilities/state parsing, not step execution.

The remaining `*.live.ru.md` files were captured on 2026-10-18 with the same components, using owned scratch features and no test client. `step`, `editor`, `results` and `state-loaded` cover a single Delay step and the editor-loaded response. `run-passed` covers execution from the middle of a scenario; `results-failed` covers an explicit, harmless exception. Paths, runner name and error date are replaced with fixed acceptance values. No business scenario or credentials are included. A long Delay stopped after approximately 2.6 seconds; Vanessa left the original run request unanswered, so KOT cancels that individual request only after observing the matching idle Broken step. Disconnect/reconnect was checked separately without closing Vanessa.

`breakpoints.live` and `run-stopped.live` cover a point at line 5. Reload clears points: restoring them after reload and using `fromCurrentStep` executed only the first Delay, then stopped before line 5. The stopped reply still has a success heading but no scenario outcome; it must remain unknown when parsed alone. A matching observed running → idle state and editor position establish the breakpoint stop in the session adapter. Probe-created points were removed afterward; unrelated points are preserved.

`breakpoints-empty.live` captures the empty list before and after a verified toggle/list/remove in a visible Monaco document. Vanessa `.45` appends “Файлы не открыты” even though the editor is open and toggle succeeds. That paragraph is advisory, not proof of editor unavailability. The session still validates file identity around every breakpoint read and confirms mutations with a fresh list. The other explicit editor-unavailable reply remains an error.

`editor-content.live` was captured from the same owned Delay-only scratch feature on 2026-10-18 using `includeContent=true`. Only paths were sanitized. The formatter adds one newline before the closing code fence; the parser retains the actual source's final newline. This permits command-time source comparison without polling or retaining scenario content in the session snapshot.

`clients.live.ru.md` captures the read-only client list on 2026-10-19, with the same `.45` components. Infobase paths and launch keys are replaced by placeholders. Neither client was connected. The three client tool schemas in `tools.live.json` come from the actual tools/list response; `tools.json` keeps those schemas too. This list fixture establishes formatting only, not live connect/disconnect/close acceptance.

`clients-connected.live.ru.md` and `client-closed.live.ru.md` capture an owned, disposable copy of the KOT service infobase on 2026-10-19. Only this client's startup/connection state was changed. Full paths, launch keys and generated profile identities are sanitized; localized PID grouping is retained. Two profiles were added and edited; connect, disconnect, reconnect and close passed through the production session/adapter. Close waits for OS process exit but the profile table retains its old PID. The original failure with the old `/NoSplash` example was a real 1C login dialog for user `oSplash`; the example is corrected to `/Lru /DisableStartupMessages`. No business client was connected or executed.

The three form tool schemas were copied from the same verified .45 tools/list capture on 2026-10-19. `form-element.live.ru.md` is the real read-only response for a checkbox on Vanessa itself, opened as an external processor in an owned copied service infobase TestClient. It contains no business data. The handler uses lowercase Russian state booleans and an English value representation. Full tree capture (1680 nodes) stays private; tests use first-party synthetic labels through that exact formatter. This does not establish UI table-row capture or interactive locator parity with the existing bridge.

The diagnostic and window-selection schemas were projected from the same real 48-tool handshake on 2026-10-20. Runtime search, syntax checking, manager log, owned-file PNG screenshot and exact test-client window activation were accepted against the owned disposable client. The `.45` screenshot response returns a file path, not an inline image; KOT supplies and reads its own temporary path for a local endpoint. Diagnostic redaction/cancellation tests use synthetic credential strings and no business data. This does not certify another EPF version.
